title: Proximity Without Community
sentences: Living physically near other people has never automatically produced a community of any kind.
What produced it historically was repeated and largely unavoidable mutual dependence.
You knew the baker because there was simply no practical alternative to knowing him.
Modern cities have removed very nearly every such compulsory encounter from daily life.
This is, by almost any measure available, a substantial gain in ordinary personal freedom.
It also dissolved the accidental relationships that freedom cannot easily replace.
Deliberate community requires effort that dependence used to supply for nothing at all.
The people who manage it tend to have spare time, which is very unevenly distributed.
So conviviality quietly becomes another good that sorts itself by household income.
We have arranged our streets so that solitude is now the default setting for everyone.
